extracted.intended_audience: Principal Investigators applying for ERC (Horizon 2020) grants
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluation standards for ERC frontier research grant applications (Starting, Consolidator, Advanced) under the ERC Work Programme 2016, including eligibility, evaluation, budgets, host institution obligations, and ethics/research integrity requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific excellence as the sole criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific excellence is the sole criterion on the basis of which ERC frontier research grants are awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research funded by the ERC is expected to lead to advances at the frontiers of knowledge and to set a clear and inspirational target for frontier research across Europe. The ERC emphasises frontier, interdisciplinary, pioneering and unconventional proposals and high-gain/high-risk research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review evaluation by panels
rubrics_metrics.description: The evaluation of ERC grant applications is conducted by peer review panels composed of renowned scientists and scholars selected by the ERC Scientific Council; panels may be assisted by independent experts working remotely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels and evaluation processes are designed to identify scientific excellence irrespective of gender, age, nationality or institution and to take career breaks and unconventional career paths into account. Evaluations are monitored to guarantee transparency, fairness and impartiality. The ERC applies rules on confidentiality and conflict of interest to ensure research integrity of the evaluation process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal completeness and scope (eligibility of proposals)
rubrics_metrics.description: All proposals must be complete and submitted before the relevant call deadline. A complete proposal entails all parts or sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incomplete proposals may be declared ineligible. The content of the proposal must relate to the objectives and to the grant type set out in the call; a proposal will only be deemed ineligible on grounds of ‘scope’ in clear-cut cases. Where there is doubt on eligibility, peer review may proceed pending an eligibility review committee decision; if an eligibility criterion is not met at any stage, the proposal will be declared ineligible and not considered further.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility of Principal Investigator (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigators of any nationality may apply and may reside in any country at time of application; Starting, Consolidator and Advanced proposals are submitted by the Principal Investigator on behalf of the host institution, who has scientific responsibility for the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principal Investigators funded through ERC grants shall spend a minimum percentage of their total working time in an EU Member State or Associated Country and a minimum percentage of their total working time on the ERC project (specific minima vary by grant type). The Principal Investigator normally will be employed by the Host Institution; exceptional situations can be accommodated subject to approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility by career stage (Starting / Consolidator / Advanced PhD windows)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific eligibility criteria based on date of award of the first PhD (or equivalent doctoral degree): Starting Grant PIs: ≥2 and ≤7 years prior to 1 January 2016; Consolidator Grant PIs: >7 and ≤12 years prior to 1 January 2016; Advanced Grant: none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reference date is the date of actual award according to national rules. The effective elapsed time since the award may be reduced in properly documented circumstances (see reduction rules). See Annex 2 for guidance on PhD equivalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction of eligibility window for documented life events
rubrics_metrics.description: The effective elapsed time since the award of the first PhD can be reduced in certain properly documented circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For maternity the elapsed time is reduced by 18 months for each child; for paternity by the documented amount of paternity leave actually taken; for long-term illness, clinical training or national service the elapsed time is reduced by the documented amount of leave actually taken for each incident which occurred after the PhD award (long-term illness defined as over ninety days for the PI or a close family member). Documentation is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible host institution
rubrics_metrics.description: The host institution (Applicant Legal Entity) must engage the Principal Investigator for at least the duration of the project and be established in an EU Member State or Associated Country or be an eligible international/EU organisation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any type of legal entity, public or private, including universities, research organisations and undertakings can host PIs. The host is expected to be the only participating legal entity unless additional entities bring scientific added value. Legal entities outside the EU/Associated Countries may participate if deemed essential. See Annex 3 for associated countries and restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host institution conditions to ensure PI independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Host institutions must provide appropriate conditions for the Principal Investigator to independently manage the research and funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions (subject of supplementary agreement) must ensure the PI is able to: apply for funding independently; manage the research and funding and make resource allocation decisions; publish independently as senior author and include co-authors only if contributed substantially; supervise team members including students; have access to appropriate space and facilities. Host must not constrain PI by institutional research strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding rates and maximum grant amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum grant varies by grant type and the Union contribution will reimburse up to 100% of eligible direct costs plus flat-rate financing of indirect costs at 25% of total eligible direct costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximum amounts (examples for 2016): Starting Grant up to EUR 1,500,000 (plus up to EUR 500,000 additional for start-up/equipment/facilities); Consolidator up to EUR 2,000,000 (plus up to EUR 750,000 additional); Advanced up to EUR 2,500,000 (plus up to EUR 1,000,000 additional). The awarded grant is a maximum overall figure; final payment must be justified on actual costs incurred. Certain exclusions to the 25% indirect calculation apply (e.g., subcontracting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget justification and panel assessment of funding requested
rubrics_metrics.description: During peer review, evaluation panels will assess the funding requested by the applicant against the needs of the project before making any recommendation for funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The funding requested must be fully justified by an estimation of the real project cost. Panels may suggest modifications to the indicative budgetary breakdown where requests are not properly justified and shall explain in writing any suggested modification. The Principal Investigator may modify the budgetary breakdown during the course of the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open access to publications (mandatory) and research data (recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Beneficiaries of ERC grants must ensure open access to all peer-reviewed scientific publications relating to project results; there is no formal obligation to provide open access to research data, but ERC recommends following best practice and being prepared to share data when not bound by restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed requirements on open access to publications are contained in the Horizon 2020 ERC Model Grant Agreement. Beneficiaries may opt-in voluntarily to the Horizon 2020 Pilot on Open Research Data, with additional obligations; they may opt out at any stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical principles and legal compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed research and innovation activities shall comply with ethical principles and relevant national, Union and international legislation, including the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the EU and the European Convention on Human Rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particular attention to proportionality, right to privacy, protection of personal data, physical and mental integrity, non-discrimination and high levels of human health protection. Research must have exclusive focus on civil applications. Funding of human embryonic stem cell research is possible within the ethical framework defined in Horizon 2020.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research integrity and sanctions for misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and promote a culture of research integrity at all stages of evaluation and granting; cases of scientific misconduct (fabrication, falsification, plagiarism, misrepresentation) will be addressed vigorously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breaches may lead to sanctions such as rejection of proposals from evaluation, requests for measures by the host institution, reduction of the grant and suspension or termination of grants. Host institutions have primary responsibility for detection, investigation and adjudication, and are expected to have structures in place and to inform the ERC of allegations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on submission of proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Restrictions apply to submissions based on the outcome of previous evaluations and other circumstances to maintain quality and integrity of the ERC evaluation process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Only the first eligible proposal per Principal Investigator submitted to different ERC frontier grant calls under the same Work Programme will be evaluated. PIs evaluated as category C in earlier Work Programmes 2014 or 2015 may not submit to 2016. PIs rejected for breach of research integrity in previous calls may not submit. A researcher may participate as PI or Co-Investigator in only one ERC frontier research project at any one time. PIs who are serving Panel Members for a 2016 call or who served in 2014 may not apply to 2016 for the same type of grant. Ineligible or withdrawn proposals do not count against these restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time commitment requirements by grant type
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigators must commit minimum percentages of their total working time in an EU Member State or Associated Country and on the ERC project; these minima are part of eligibility and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Starting Grant PIs: minimum 50% of total working time in EU/Associated Country and minimum 50% on the ERC project. Consolidator Grant PIs: minimum 50% in EU/Associated Country and minimum 40% on the ERC project. Time commitment is monitored and insufficient commitment may lead to reduction of grant, suspension or termination per the grant agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track record / expected early achievements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must demonstrate track record appropriate to field and career stage; specific listing requirements are defined in the Track Record section of the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Starting Grant: list up to five publications in major international peer-reviewed multidisciplinary journals and/or leading journals/conference proceedings/monographs, highlighting those without PhD supervisor as co-author, and citation counts (excluding self-citations); may include monographs, granted patents, invited presentations, prizes/awards/academy memberships. Consolidator Grant: similar list up to ten publications. Advanced Grant: expected significant achievements in last ten years; benchmarks may include 10 publications as senior author (or joint author where alphabetic norm), 3 major research monographs (with translations), 5 granted patents, leadership in launching careers, recognized industrial innovation leadership, invited presentations, research expeditions, organisation of international conferences, etc. Track Record sections request up to ten representative publications from the last ten years for Advanced applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation criteria and scoring for other Horizon 2020 actions
rubrics_metrics.description: For actions under 'other parts' (non-frontier-grants) evaluation criteria are: 1. Excellence; 2. Impact; 3. Quality and efficiency of the implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example assessment questions: Excellence — Are the objectives consistent with the work programme/call and do they go beyond best practice? Impact — Will the project have substantial impact in the context of ERC objectives? Quality and efficiency of implementation — Is methodology and work plan effective in reaching goals and ensuring highest quality/utility of results? Each criterion is marked 0–5 and an overall quality threshold of 80% is used to establish the retained list of proposals which will be ranked for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel structure and panel assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: ERC uses a panel structure covering Physical Sciences & Engineering, Life Sciences and Social Sciences & Humanities with detailed descriptors (PE1–PE10, LS1–LS9, SH1–SH6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should select the appropriate panel corresponding to their research area (panel descriptions list the fields covered, e.g., PE6 Computer Science and Informatics; LS3 Cellular and Developmental Biology; SH4 Cognitive science, psychology, linguistics, philosophy of mind). Call budgets are allocated to panels in proportion to budgetary demand of assigned proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portability of ERC grants
rubrics_metrics.description: ERC grants are portable as described in the ERC Model Grant Agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portability means the Principal Investigator may request to transfer the entire grant or part of it to a new beneficiary under specific Model Grant Agreement conditions. These conditions may include provisions for transfer of equipment purchased and used exclusively for the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bottom-up approach and eligible scientific fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be made in any field of research; ERC frontier research grants operate on a 'bottom-up' basis without predetermined priorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ERC encourages interdisciplinary proposals crossing boundaries, pioneering proposals addressing new/emerging fields, or proposals introducing unconventional, innovative approaches and scientific inventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of Concept grants availability
rubrics_metrics.description: ERC Principal Investigators will continue to be able to apply for Proof of Concept Grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof of Concept call identifiers, opening dates, deadlines and indicative budgets are provided in the Work Programme. (Further detailed PoC eligibility and evaluation rules are contained in the specific call texts and Model Grant Agreement.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Union contribution and financial rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The Union financial contribution reimburses up to 100% of total eligible and approved direct costs plus flat-rate financing of indirect costs at 25% of total eligible direct costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The awarded grant represents a maximum overall figure — the final amount to be paid must be justified on the basis of costs actually incurred for the project. Certain exclusions apply to the 25% calculation (excluding direct costs for subcontracting and costs of resources made available by third parties not used on the host premises). Budget figures and call budgets are indicative and subject to availability of appropriations; final budgets may vary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host institution responsibilities for research integrity checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Host institutions that engage ERC Principal Investigators have primary responsibility for detection, investigation and adjudication of scientific misconduct and for ensuring no pending allegations exist against applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Host institutions are expected to have structures in place to uphold research integrity and to make appropriate efforts to verify that no allegations of misconduct are pending against any PI applying for or participating in an ERC grant and to bring such allegations to the attention of the ERC.
